mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST QoQ change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of at least 0.4 percentage points from the previous month, sustained for two consecutive months, indicates deteriorating labor market conditions, which historically precede negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by >= 0.4pp for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such UNRATE episodes (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals contraction in manufacturing output, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such INDPRO contraction episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual monetary inflation and tightening shock, which historically drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days due to short-term risk-on sentiment.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such dual shocks (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a concurrent decline in personal consumption expenditures growth (proxied by GDPC1 growth), signals a shift from spending to saving, which historically precedes negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-mo MA AND GDPC1 growth < 0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during such episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive correlation between payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) and S&P 500 returns exists: when monthly PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.3%, S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days are expected to be positive.
failure_condition: When PAYEMS growth exceeds 0.3% monthly, S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) over out-of-sample periods.

mechanism_narrative: During periods when both industrial production (INDPRO) and housing starts (HOUST) rise above their respective 6-month moving averages simultaneously, supply-side expansion is likely to boost corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive during such joint expansions (t-test p > 0.05).
